And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

Arsenal are more likely to "seriously consider" a move to sign RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa next summer than they are in January, sources have told Football Insider.

The Gunners are long-term admirers of the Norway international, but are expected to find Leipzig difficult to negotiate with this winter.

The German side are determined not to lose Nusa mid-season, especially given they are still competing in the Champions League.

Sources say that their star's £66million price tag will also be prohibitive for Arsenal given the hectic nature of the January window.

However, a summer move to the Premier League is seen as being much "more likely" for the 21-year-old, with Arsenal set to continue tracking him.

Mikel Arteta is desperate to add another left-sided forward to his attack, and Nusa is seen as the perfect fit for the role when he becomes available.

Nusa has enjoyed a remarkable rise since he first joined Leipzig back in 2024, and he has taken his game to new heights already this term.

The wideman has firmly established himself as Leipzig's prized asset, and already has four goals and seven assists from just nine Bundesliga games in 2026-27.

Nusa is even closely matching Ballon D'Or winger Harry Kane, who is just one goal involvement ahead of him at the top of the Bundesliga charts.

The starlet has been continually linked with a move to the Premier League throughout the last 12 months, but Leipzig remain determined to sell him on their terms.

He is under contract with them until the summer of 2029, and that is allowing them to hold out for a lofty fee for him.

Arsenal will have to splash the cash to sign Nusa, but that may be something they are prepared to do next summer.

Football Insider revealed earlier this week that Arsenal are keen to make a move to sign QPR's teenage sensation Leon Scarlett.

The 17-year-old has caught the attention of several clubs of late, after breaking into the Hoops' first-team this season.

Brighton and Rangers are also closely monitoring Scarlett's progress, and the British trio feel that theey could steal a march on their rivals.

Scarlett's age will prevent him from moving to a European club until next summer, giving Arsenal and Co. an advance window to strike a deal.

#1987. Newcastle: Expert 'had to laugh' after what he heard about Lewis Hall and Matthias Jaissle

Matthias Jaissle has reportedly been told that Lewis Hall will not be sold in the January transfer window, but it should be his own position at Newcastle United that he is worried about.

That is the opinion of experienced former Tottenham, Everton and Aston Villa scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The 22-year-old has enjoyed an incredibly impressive start to the season and was superb against Lamine Yamal as England beat Spain 3-2 last week.

Hall attracted significant interest from Manchester United in the summer transfer window but eventually committed his future to Newcastle in September, putting pen to paper on terms until 2031.

The Red Devils remain interested and other clubs are likely to join them, despite the Magpies' determined stance on any potential sale.

The left-back spoke of belief in Jaissle's project when he signed, but the German now finds himself under real pressure after a disappointing start to the campaign.

🚨Newcastle United told Matthias Jaissle this morning that Lewis Hall was not for salehttps://t.co/spGrAf37PJ #nufc #mufc

Hall's loyalty to Newcastle is yet to waiver, but he will undoubtedly have aspirations that go beyond Champions League qualification.

It is up to the Magpies to match them because if they do not, another club certainly will.

"That was a wise move by Newcastle to get him tied up because he's going to cost a lot of money, that kid," King told Football Insider.

"The question will be, is he going to be loyal to Newcastle? But on the other end, are they going to win anything? I had to laugh when I read an article about Jaissle.

"They said that they told him that Lewis Hall would remain at the football club and he wouldn't be sold in January. Well, is that manager going to be there in January?

"They've let three of their best players go since they won the League Cup. And that's [Alexander] Isak, [Sandro] Tonali and [Bruno] Guimaraes.

"A lot of money, £300million there for three players. Now, that was decent recruitment."

Newcastle will hope to pick up after the international break despite winning just three of their opening 10 Premier League games.

It will not get much easier, however, with Arsenal, Brighton and Man United all to come in the next few weeks.

"It's been a weird season so far, I think we've shown in spells what a good team we can be," Hall said last week.

"We've got a young squad, which is only going to get better and better. I think it's difficult, the situation we're in at the minute, but we're working really hard in training and we're really looking forward to what's coming.”

#1986. Jordan Pickford told not to quit Everton after being axed - ex-employee

Jordan Pickford should not be thinking about a move away from Everton with his England place under threat.

That is according to former senior Everton scout and Millwall goalkeeper, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The 32-year-old has been England's number one for countless years, earning 94 caps, but his shirt now looks to be under threat.

James Trafford started against Spain on Sunday and was superb, with some now suggesting that he has usurped Pickford in the England goal.

The Leeds United keeper offers far more with his feet and gave an great example of his shot-stopping ability on Sunday, too, making two excellent double saves.

It remains to be seen whether Thomas Tuchel does now see Pickford as his number two, with the England boss playing down such talk after the game.

James Trafford last-gasp double save 🤯🤯#UNLSaves | @Betano_PT pic.twitter.com/K3Rn995OEE

For years, there have been suggestions that Pickford could leave Everton for a bigger club.

But the 32-year-old has never had a reason to, with his position in the England team never in question.

Now, for the first time in a long time, it is, and the thought that Pickford could push to join a bigger club to win it back has entered some minds.

"Why would he push for a move? He's playing first team football, where he is," King told Football Insider when asked about the idea.

"If he's going to get his England place back, he's got to be playing games. His Everton place is not under threat. He's got to play first team football to keep in the frame for an England place.

"There's a shortage of England goalkeepers, let's be fair. There is a shortage. When you've got one who was, who was number two at one time, Nick Pope.

"All of a sudden, he's number three at Newcastle. Then you've got [Dean] Henderson at Palace. You've got Trafford. You've got Pickford. There isn't much that springs to mind as top English goalkeepers."

Speaking after the clash against Spain, Tuchel was keen to play down the idea of an established number one.

"There is no need for a new number one. It’s a good double save. That’s what we wanted," the German said.

"He [Trafford] had a brilliant match. It only works if you’re top from number one to 11. [He was] very good. That’s his job, to close the gap.

"We want competition in all positions. We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments. The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant."

#1985. South American trips and rejected approaches: What Arne Slot has been doing since Liverpool exit

It’s now coming up to six months since Arne Slot was relieved of his duties as Liverpool head coach after two years in the role.

The Dutchman had the unenviable task of succeeding Jurgen Klopp in the Anfield dugout but delivered a surprise (and emphatic) Premier League title triumph in his first season in charge before the Reds’ fortunes nosedived dramatically last term.

The 48-year-old just about managed to achieve Champions League qualification in May, but the extent of the decline from 12 months previously made his position untenable, and he was dismissed to make way for Andoni Iraola.

In his latest Liverpool Confidential feature for the Daily Mail, Lewis Steele addressed the question of what Slot has been getting up to since his exit from Anfield, with the journalist ‘often asked’ about the Dutch tactician’s more recent endeavours.

He outlined that the former Reds boss has been ‘biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones’, including multiple trips to Ibiza and taking in football matches in Argentina and Brazil with his son Joep, along with attending games in his native Netherlands.

The 48-year-old turned down the chance to coach his country after the World Cup, as well as potentially ‘lucrative gig’ in Saudi Arabia. He also declined approaches from a few clubs in the summer, including AC Milan, who now have ex-Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim in charge.

Steele concluded that Slot is ‘waiting for the right opportunity’ to get back into the dugout and doesn’t believe that his ‘stock has fallen’ as much as some of his peers who’ve been sacked by other high-profile Premier League clubs.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The Dutchman’s Liverpool tenure may have ended on a low ebb, and the prevailing sentiment in May was that the time was right for a change, but it’d be wrong to describe his two-year spell at Anfield as a failure.

He vastly exceeded expectations by winning the Premier League at the first attempt, and while last season was undoubtedly a massive underachievement results-wise, it must be viewed in the context of Slot and the squad trying to navigate the horrendous grief of Diogo Jota’s tragic death.

That the 48-year-old has turned down job approaches in order to hold out for the ‘right opportunity’ indicates his confidence that he’ll get back on board the managerial carousel sooner rather than later, and that his reputation hasn’t been overly tarnished by the disappointment of 2025/26.

Most Liverpool fans would also acknowledge that Slot carried himself with tremendous dignity throughout his time with us, striking the perfect tone with his farewell message to supporters after his sacking and – most importantly – handling the loss of Jota with commendable grace.

It’s nice to hear that the Dutchman has been enjoying his time with family since departing Merseyside, and it wouldn’t surprise us in the slightest if he were to be back in the technical area with a new club over the next few months.

Wherever his career might take him from here, we wish him the best in his future endeavours.

#1984. Man City will regret how they have 'treated' James Trafford - ex-goalkeeper

James Trafford was treated at Manchester City in a similar way to how Joe Hart was 10 years ago.

That is according to experienced former Everton, Tottenham and Aston Villa scout and former professional goalkeeper, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The 24-year-old has impressed this season after he was sold to Leeds United in a deal worth up to £45million in the summer transfer window, just a year after returning to the club.

Man City had re-signed Trafford from Burnley after utilising their matching rights clause, with the expectation being that he would be their new number one following Ederson's exit.

But just weeks after his return had been confirmed, transfer chiefs at the Etihad Stadium spied an opportunity to sign Gianluigi Donnarumma from PSG and did so.

The Italy international instantly became the number one in the Premier League and the Champions League, with Trafford resigned to appearances in the cup competitions.

In the 2015-16 season, Hart made 47 appearances for Man City and was England's number one goalkeeper.

But Pep Guardiola's arrival in the summer of 2016 changed everything. Hart was loaned out to Torino and initially replaced by Claudio Bravo, before Ederson arrived in 2017.

The Englishman would go on to play for West Ham on loan, before playing for Burnley, Tottenham and Celtic until his retirement in 2024.

"They followed the handling of him as they did with Joe Hart, it's the same treatment," King told Football Insider when asked about Man City's treatment of Trafford.

"Joe Hart was England number one, and for some reason [they said]: 'He isn't good enough. We're bringing in the Brazilian keeper, Ederson.'

"Then Joe Hart leaves the football club and goes to Celtic and wins loads of cups and leagues and everything up there. He's now a pundit and a good one.

"He had his career pushed out, and it didn't help the standard of goalkeeping in England, did it? He was England's number one and all of a sudden, he wasn't good enough for Man City.

"Because of the reason we've been talking about - his feet. That's why he got replaced, because they wanted to bring the Brazilian boy because he was good with his feet."

Leaving Man City has been momentous for Trafford, who is now in contention to be in England's number one after an impressive start with Leeds.

And with Donnarumma attracting criticism this season, their treatment of their former academy player may well be something looked back on with regret.

"What a horrendous, horrendous feeling. Not playing," Trafford told BBC Sport. "You are ringing a lot of people and just venting.

"Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up. I ring my dad, I ring my mum, I ring my missus, I ring my mates. I like ringing my mates and we can just have a good talk about it all. It's quite funny.

"I had to play regularly this season for my own mental wellbeing. You just lose yourself not playing. Maybe I'm different, I don't know, but the feeling of not playing every week, it felt horrendous."

"I just had to play every week this season for that mental feel-good and to keep progressing with my career and edging me closer to achieving the dreams I want to achieve."

#1983. Grief-stricken Tenerife stars return to action for first time since death of Jesus de Miguel, 30, after fatal on-field collision with goalkeeper: Tributes paid and match paused in 9th minute on emotional day

Published: 14:11 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 21:21 EST, 15 November 2026

Tenerife have returned to action for the first time since Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel was tragically killed in a collision during a game with FC Andorra earlier this month.

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out De Miguel with a high challenge, which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

Thirteen days on from the incident, Tenerife played their first game since the player's death as they took on AD Ceuta CF in LaLiga Hypermotion action – with the game filled with tributes to the star.

Players gave a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – the shirt number he wore.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars, meanwhile, took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the incident.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of De Miguel before the game kicked off.

🕊️❤️ THE NINTH MINUTE BELONGED TO JESÚS DE MIGUEL! 🥹🏟️ Football took a back seat during Tenerife's first match following his passing.👏 In the ninth minute, the stadium came together in a heartfelt tribute to honor his memory.💔 Some losses are felt far beyond the pitch.… pic.twitter.com/mqPy4aE9Q3

CF Tenerife returned to action for the first time since the death of Jesus de Miguel in a game flooded with tributes

Both sets of players gathered around the centre circle before the game to pay tribute

The forward (pictured in 2025) passed away after being on the receiving end of a brutal tackle

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'

Other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, De Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place De Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

The tragedy occurred as the game against Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture. Fans have chanted 'murderer' in his direction.

Before the game, players gathered outside gate nine - the shirt numebr de Miguel wore

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban and may never play football again

On Friday, the goalkeeper was hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

His manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'

#1982. Chelsea news: Estevao Willian provides fresh comments on playing time frustration after latest Brazil appearance

By Darren Plant | 17 Nov 2026 20:14

Chelsea winger Estevao Willian has thanked Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti for his "trust" during the international break.

The 19-year-old's lack of starts for Chelsea since the arrival of Xabi Alonso has been a regular topic of conversation.

Although the Spaniard placed more faith in the playmaker prior to the November international break, Estevao was still dropped after an encouraging performance versus Manchester United on October 31.

However, Ancelotti has recently insisted that Estevao's game time for Chelsea will not negatively impact on his role for the national team.

That stance has since been proven through the former Palmeiras starlet featuring for 128 minutes across friendlies versus Japan and Singapore.

During Tuesday's 7-0 win over Singapore, Estevao contributed one goal and two assists before his 70th-minute withdrawal.

Speaking to ESPN after the game, Estevao admitted that he was grateful for the support that he had received from Ancelotti.

He said: "I'm very happy to have gotten minutes in the friendlies.

"I thank Ancelotti for his confidence, because every player wants to play and at Chelsea I've had few minutes, but coming here and knowing that the manager trusts me gives me a lot of motivation."

With Kallang - the venue for Tuesday's friendly - eight hours in front of England, Estevao is essentially getting extra rest ahead of Saturday's Premier League game versus Leeds United.

Nevertheless, not only will it take his body clock time to reset, the likes of Cole Palmer, Danny Welbeck and Emanuel Emegha - players competing for roles in the final third - have not represented their countries during the international break.

Meanwhile, Morgan Rogers was back in the country on Monday after representing England, so Estevao is essentially at a disadvantage when it comes to trying to dislodge teammates from the starting lineup.

All things considered, it is highly likely that he will take a place on the substitutes' bench.

#1981. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Your Addicks to take on Spurs 🏆#cafc pic.twitter.com/uyH4dfH9CD

Our Spurs side to face Charlton! 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/yQuEVgkHbm

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1980. Liverpool training: Four Reds players provide Iraola with timely boost ahead of Man United clash

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has been provided with a timely team news boost ahead of the Premier League showdown against Manchester United on Sunday.

With the international break now concluded, the Reds players who were away with their countries have now reconvened on Merseyside and were put through their paces at the AXA Training Centre on Thursday.

There were no fresh injury concerns arising from national team duties, and there had already been good news earlier in the week when Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni resumed first-team training as they both close in on long-awaited returns from lengthy absences.

As per Liverpool Echo, a number of Reds players who had been carrying slight knocks or been absent through injury prior to the international window are now on course to be available for the Man United fixture.

The Dutch trio of Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong all trained, with the captain skipping Netherlands duty due to a minor issue, the midfielder missing our last three games with a heel problem, and the right-back overcoming a muscle injury he sustained in mid-October.

Dominik Szoboszlai had played through a slight knee problem for Hungary in recent days, but he was involved in the session in Kirkby today, albeit with strapping on the affected area.

Two other notable inclusions were Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo, both of whom partook in training despite being just back from representing their countries in South America, although Bradley and Leoni weren’t involved in today’s session as their recoveries are being managed carefully.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Iraola will be delighted to get through the international window with no fresh injury absentees (unlike the damaging extended break earlier in the autumn), and also to see those who had been carrying knocks all involved in the session this morning.

The returns of Gravenberch and Frimpong give the head coach greater scope for selection in midfield and at right-back respectively, and Van Dijk and Szoboszlai could both be cleared to start as they seem to have shaken off their minor issues.

Barring any new setbacks between now and Sunday, it looks as though the only definite absentees for the Man United game will be Bradley, Leoni and Hugo Ekitike, each of whom continue to nurse long-term injuries but are on course to return in the coming weeks.

Iraola will inevitably be asked for updates on each of those players when he holds his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon, and his squad seems to be nicely stocked at the beginning of what’ll be a punishing fixture schedule in the lead-up to the festive period. Long may it stay that way!

#1977. Tottenham urged to sign £12.5m midfielder who would be "top five" in Premier League

By Ben Knapton | 17 Nov 2026 20:21, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 20:21

Tottenham Hotspur have been urged to make an approach for AC Milan midfielder Youssouf Fofana, who could be one of the "top five" players in his position in the Premier League.

The Lilywhites spent big to reinforce their engine room during the summer with the signings of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes for a combined £185m, while Rodrigo Bentancur, Lucas Bergvall and Conor Gallagher remain on the books too.

However, a report from Italian outlet Calciomercato states that Tottenham are 'ready to attack' for Fofana, who is currently on loan at Sevilla from Milan and has made a positive impression in La Liga.

Fofana has scored one goal and provided three assists in nine Spanish top-flight appearances, but he is only under contract with Milan until 2028, and his long-term future remains unclear.

Speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, former Milan striker Mark Hateley implored Tottenham to make a move for Fofana, whom he believes everyone would be casting their eye on if he became available.

"That's the type of player all top clubs would look for, even as a bit-part player," Hateley said. "He's one of those players who'll get into the side and be good in it, and then out of the side if need be.

“There are a lot better players out there, but he is a good player. That's the difference between the top three, four, five clubs now. You can pay £50m or £60m for a guy who's just going to be knocking around the squad, and that's where we are in the football world right now.

“He'd be one of the top three, four or five in England anyway; we'd all be looking at that sort of player if he became available.

“Spurs are still struggling to find something at the moment. It's normally the player you never imagine is going to make everybody else work: the squad player, your £30m or £40m, maybe £50m player, and it works.

“That's where we are with Tottenham right now. I've seen them play very well this season, but I've also seen them play very, very poorly, and that's the frustration with supporters, because you don't know which team is going to turn up. It's not an 11 you're building right now, it's an 18 or 19-man starting line-up."

Reportedly valued at just £12.5m by AC Milan, Fofana does not trump his Spurs rivals in many statistical columns, but the 27-year-old is superior to Fernandes, Tonali, Gallagher and Bentancur on a few metrics.

Fofana's 0.38 assists per 90 minutes is the highest total among the quintet, as is his 1.15 successful dribbles per game, from 3.56 attempts; Gallagher is second in the latter statistic with 1.42.

Fofana has also been dispossessed on the fewest occasions - just 0.76 times per 90 minutes - and was no stranger to a direct involvement during his first two seasons with Milan.

The ex-Monaco man has scored three goals and set up 13 more in 88 games for the Rossoneri, although he was left out of France's World Cup squad and has not represented Les Bleus since 2024.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.Bet.

#1970. Liverpool games v Man United and Everton moved as Premier League confirm updated fixture details

Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.

With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.

The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.

On Thursday, the Premier League announced updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool’s games being moved.

The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage.

The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The new dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January.

Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield.

*FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December

**If Liverpool advance to Carabao Cup semi-finals

The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we’ll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won’t be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Liverpool currently have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month.

It’s quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two).

Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.

#1969. Wayne Rooney opens up on mental health struggles, drinking and seeking help from a therapist

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 20:39

Wayne Rooney has revealed that he contemplated suicide during his time at Manchester United. The former England captain, 41, spoke about it on the Life at the Midpoint podcast, hosted by Gabby Logan, describing a period when his eldest son Kai was still a baby. The interview was reported by the BBC and also picked up by Sky Sports.

‘I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide,’ Rooney said. ‘You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.’

Rooney was speaking about years when he was at his best on the pitch. According to the BBC, Kai is now 17, so the period was roughly 17 years ago. He describes it as a time when he had just got married and just had a son.

‘It should be the happiest point in my life, and it wasn’t,’ he said. Asked by Logan about the hardest moment of his life, he said that when he was drinking he would shut himself at home for two days and just drink, at what was probably the best phase of his career in playing terms.

He joined United from Everton in 2004 and, according to the BBC, became the club’s all-time top scorer with 253 goals in 559 games. He won five Premier League titles, the Champions League, the Europa League, the FA Cup and three League Cups before returning to Everton in 2017. He remains a legend at Old Trafford, where Mauricio Pochettino is now beginning his time as boss.

‘I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, I really struggled with it,’ he said on the podcast.

Rooney also explained why nothing showed on the outside at the time. ‘You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,’ he said. He said a feeling that he would be less of a man stopped him admitting his own state. In the end he confided in his wife Coleen and his mother and started speaking to a therapist. He now describes his behaviour at the time as selfish. ‘Coleen helped me enormously,’ he added. ‘She could have left, it was that bad, but she stayed by me and helped me get through it.’

This is not the first time Rooney has spoken about a dark period. In February 2022, when the Rooney documentary came out on Amazon Prime Video and he was managing Derby County, he told the PA news agency, as reported by The42, that he suffered inside for a long part of his career and that a lot of it ended in drinking. He also told the Mail on Sunday, as reported by Inside World Football, that in his early years at United, until about the birth of Kai, he would shut himself at home and drink. He pointed to the pressure of playing for England and United and what the newspapers wrote about his private life. According to PA, he saw a psychologist only briefly at the time.

The new interview is a significant step on from those earlier accounts. In the 2022 pieces, the subjects were alcohol and the pressure of fame, with no mention of suicidal thoughts. Rooney did, however, explain then why he stayed silent as a player. He said he could not go to older players such as Roy Keane or Ryan Giggs and say there was a problem. He added that today it is much easier, because mental health is talked about and problems are caught earlier, especially among young players.

England’s most famous striker of his generation could not speak about his state while he was playing, and speaks most openly about it as a former player and television pundit. He has been named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards and currently appears in the ITV reality show I’m a Celebrity. The subject has remained relevant in dressing rooms, as goalkeeper James Trafford showed recently when he left Manchester City over his mental health.

If you or someone you know is struggling, support is available. In the UK, Samaritans can be called free at any time on 116 123.

#1967. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

There is a fairly extensive video explanation of the format currently taking place. We should you be bringing you some fixtures very shortly...

The draw is now getting underway. Uefa deputy general secretary Giorgio Marchetti comes on stage to oversee proceedings. A reminder of the format:

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

CONFIRMED: #UCLdraw pots for the league phase 👀 pic.twitter.com/LpMjiap6RF

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

But before the draw we will be hearing from Villa about the 2011 final, which he scored in as Barcelona dismantled Manchester United at Wembley.

He calls it a “great generation” of players, mentioning Lionel Messi, who also scored in the 3-1 win.

Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

We’re hearing from Henry now about losing the 2006 Champions League final with Arsenal and winning three years later with Barcelona.

He’s now discussing the current Arsenal crop and how they are getting closer to the trophy. He says if “they keep their core” and make some additions they can get over the line. But PSG “are an annoying team at the moment”.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

CONFIRMED: #UCLdraw pots for the league phase 👀 pic.twitter.com/LpMjiap6RF

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

There are five English teams involved in the Champions League this season – one short of the Premier League’s tally from last term.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Liverpool will be in pot one, while Manchester United and Aston Villa will be in pot two.

This evening’s ceremony should be getting underway in Monaco in a couple of minutes.

All set for this evening's #UCL draw in Monaco 📌🏆 pic.twitter.com/N3verDUO9y

Paris St-Germain will be aiming to become the first team to win three successive Champions Leagues since Real Madrid’s run of titles between 2016 and 2018.

The holders 🔴🔵#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/eB05BNfWZi

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

Gabriel misses his penalty ❌PSG WIN THE UEFA CHAMPIONS LEAGUE!!! 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/6XSuU3xqsN

Cristiano Ronaldo 🖐️#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/WzeWLfEomZ

Mattéo Guendouzi, the former Arsenal fireband, was at the heart of chaotic and ugly scenes in the Champions League qualifying play-off between Lyon and his side Fenerbahce, culminating in a brawl at the mouth of the tunnel.

Guendouzi provoked Lyon fans as he slowly made his way off the pitch in the aftermath of a 2-1 victory at the Groupama Stadium that sent the Turkish outfit through to the Champions League group stage.

Matteo Guendouzi has not forgotten who his rivals are... 👀The former Marseille player made his feelings known as Fenerbahce knocked out Marseille's rivals Lyon. pic.twitter.com/pjDKPqPzZD

As he gestured towards the fans, while being shepherded by team-mates, objects were thrown from the crowd. A figure in what appears to be a Lyon tracksuit then emerged from the tunnel and seemed to try to aim a flying kick at Guendouzi.

Of the 36 teams in the draw, 29 qualified at the end of last season, while the remaining seven places were decided by play-offs.

AEK, LASK, Viking, Slovan Bratislava, Sabah Baku, Fenerbahce and Bodo/Glimt were the seven teams to come through the play-offs.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January. The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

#1964. Mauricio Pochettino swaps one football for another as new Man United boss continues US farewell tour at NFL clash ahead of final game in charge

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 22:54 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 22:55 EST, 15 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued on Sunday night with a pitstop at an NFL showdown.

The manager has one game left in charge of the United States before parting ways with the national team to join Manchester United after agreeing a deal with the Premier League club earlier this week.

The Argentine will replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half year contract after United agreed to pay more than £10million ($13m) to buy him and his backroom staff out of their contracts with the US Soccer Federation.

Before his return to England, the 54-year-old is enjoying his swansong with the US. In between overseeing his final games in charge of the national team, Pochettino was spotted soaking in the action of the other variety of football.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss attended the primetime NFL showdown between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio on Sunday night.

The head coach, sporting his blue USSF coat, was captured standing on the sidelines with members of his staff ahead of the Sunday Night Football matchup.

USMNT and future Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is at the Bengals-Steelers game 😭🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/B7Irn0YLnd

Mauricio Pochettino's United States farewell tour continued at the NFL on Sunday night

The new Manchester United boss attended the Cincinnati Bengals' game at Paycor Stadium

He was greeted by kicker Evan McPherson, long snapper William Wagner and punter Ryan Rehkow - members of the Bengals' special teams - on the turf before kickoff.

The US is set to face Haiti in the second-leg of their CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

The game, which will take place around a mile north of the Bengals' Paycor Stadium, will mark Pochettino's final match in charge of the US national team.

He also took charge of the USA's 6-0 first-leg win against Haiti on Tuesday, which marked the first stop on his farewell tour.

Pochettino will begin his new role with Manchester United on Wednesday, immediately following Tuesday's second-leg. His first game will be against Liverpool at Anfield next Sunday.

He emotionally addressed his departure from the US setup and impending new job in a press conference on Friday.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

The Argentine was captured on the sidelines ahead of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

#1962. Arsenal lock down defence as Hincapie joins Rice and Raya in contract talks

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 20:53

Arsenal are in advanced talks with Piero Hincapie over a new contract, according to the BBC, despite the defender having more than four years left on his current deal. The Ecuador international, 24, is the third key player to be tied down in a single week after Declan Rice and David Raya. BBC football correspondent Sami Mokbel says he is set to sign a 12-month extension on improved terms even if he is strongly linked to Barcelona in the last weeks.

On Monday evening, Sky Sports News reported that Rice, 27, had verbally agreed a new deal with Arsenal. On Tuesday morning, Sky Sports, citing The Athletic, reported in its live coverage that goalkeeper Raya, 31, had also agreed a new long-term contract. His current deal runs to 2028, and the Spaniard has won the last three Premier League Golden Gloves, according to Sky. The report came shortly after Raya admitted he would one day like to play in La Liga.

Arsenal have not officially announced any of the agreements, but the BBC says the club are preparing to confirm new contracts for Rice, Raya and Jurrien Timber. Riccardo Calafiori, 24, is also next in line, according to the BBC. The Italian left-back, who joined from Bologna in 2024, has a contract until the summer of 2029, and the club want to begin talks with him in the not-too-distant future.

Hincapie joined on 1 September 2025 from Bayer Leverkusen on a season-long loan with an option. The BBC reported at the time that Arsenal had agreed a £45m fee for a permanent deal, and saw the Ecuadorian as a direct replacement for Jakub Kiwior, who left on loan for Porto. Boss Mikel Arteta introduced him on the club website, saying: ‘Piero is physically really impressive, and his versatility and tactical flexibility give us strong options in defence.’

On 25 June 2026, the club announced they had exercised the option and the move became permanent from 1 July, without disclosing the fee. According to Arsenal, Hincapie made 39 appearances in all competitions in the title-winning season, was the club’s player of the month in February and April, and scored his only goal in February at Wolverhampton Wanderers. The defence he slotted into conceded the fewest Premier League goals for the third season running, according to the club.

The BBC now gives 47 appearances for Arsenal in total, which suggests he has added eight this season. One of them was the November game in Prague, where Arsenal beat Slavia Prague 2-1.

The Hincapie deal is not a protection against losing him for free, as that risk does not exist with more than four years remaining. A one-year extension on better terms looks mostly a reward and a way of aligning his wages with the role he has in the squad. He has gone within a year from a loan replacement for Kiwior to a player the BBC lists among the key members of Arteta’s squad.

The common thread in all three cases is timing. Rice had 18 months plus an option left, according to Sky, Raya had a deal to 2028 and Hincapie more than four years. Arsenal are not negotiating under pressure from expiring contracts, which sends a clear signal that, after the title, they want to build on the existing core. In Raya’s case there is also a defensive logic, as the goalkeeper himself opened the subject of Spain and a new contract makes such temptations more expensive. If Timber is added, and Calafiori in the coming months, Arteta will have a goalkeeper, three defenders and the driving force of midfield all on new contracts.
