Jaissle records his first ever Premier League win, heaping more misery upon Tottenham, who begin the season with two defeats. Excellent second-half finishes from Elanga and Wissa have given the visitors a superb three points in the capital.

YOU MAGSSSS! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/PRM8yYg7Yl

Barnes attempts to latch onto a ball in behind, but Kinsky races out to claim. Spurs then almost half-heartedly come forward as Udogie tries to find Marmoush with a powerful cross. The new Spurs forward gets some contact on the ball, but it ricochets to Hall, who hacks it clear. Newcastle then make a late change as Toure replaces Barnes.

Fernandes clips a pinpoint cross into Marmoush. The Egyptian shoots via a first-time volley, but his tame attempt is easily gathered by Hornicek.

Van de Ven’s reintegration into Spurs’ defence hasn’t proved helpful. The hosts have been all at sea at the back since the restart. Newcastle showed little attacking ambition in the first half but have ripped Tottenham apart in the second.

Jaissle makes another double change as both goal-scorers, Elanga and Wissa, are taken off for Murphy and Ramsey. Elanga and Wissa have both produced extremely positive displays to kickstart their seasons under their new head coach.

Spurs have looked way off the pace in this second half and Newcastle are well worth their lead on the basis of their performance since the break.

The away fans sarcastically cheer as Tonali is withdrawn for Solanke. The former Newcastle midfielder has struggled against his old club, drastically failing to impact the game.

The visitors are in dreamland! Hall swings in a corner and Woltemade towers above Udogie to win the header. The ball breaks to Wissa, who fires a delightful acrobatic finish into the net, extending Newcastle’s advantage. Spurs’ crisis deepens. They’re on course for two defeats to start the season.

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

And this time it is another two of last summer’s signings who have combined for Newcastle United’s second goal of the afternoon.

Nick Woltemade won the initial header and got the assist a few seconds after replacing Joe Willock, but what a finish from Yoane Wissa, an improvised overhead flick from close range.

Newcastle needed Elanga and Wissa to be far better this season than they were in their first campaign on Tyneside and both of them have been electric so far under Matthias Jaissle.

As for Sandro Tonali, Newcastle saw this version of the Italy international all too often in his final season at St James’ Park. Good engine, runs around a lot, but does not influence the game in any meaningful way. A reminder Spurs spent £100m on him and have spent almost £400m in total this summer. They have been abject in the second half.

Porro tries his luck from range but Hornicek is there for Newcastle to tip the ball over the bar. The visitors then make a double change as Steur and Woltemade replace Nico and Willock.

De Zerbi makes a triple change as Spurs look to find a way back into this match. Robertson, Gray and Tel depart for Udogie, Moore and Kudus.

Spurs have a free kick in a dangerous position, but Tel slips as he goes to shoot and it flies well over the bar. That sums up Tottenham’s evening so far.

That makes two goals in two games for Elanga, who scored zero Premier League goals last season. It’s an outstanding finish, on the spin while falling backwards. It prompted some great noises from the away end, too, as the ball seemed to cross the line in slow motion.

The visitors have started his second half well and fly into the lead. Nico switches the play and picks out Dedic with a precise long-ball. The full-back cushions a header into Elanga, who swivels and slides a low effort in off the post to open the scoring and send the away support into a euphoric sea of celebration. What answers do Spurs and De Zerbi have now?

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

Newcastle deserved that goal. They have been the stronger side since the halftime interval, and this is the Anthony Elanga that Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer.

He scored on the opening weekend against Liverpool, but this was an even better finish, spinning sharply and sweeping a shot home on the turn. Smart dance moves for the celebration too.

It all came about from another long diagonal ball forward, but this time it was inch perfect from Nico Gonzalez for Harvey Barnes to put a header into the path of Elanga inside the box.

Newcastle are really growing into this contest, with Spurs getting deeper and deeper. Elanga is starting to get some joy out wide.

The momentum has arguably been with Newcastle since the interval. They’re pushing Spurs back towards their own goal. The visitors are waiting to fashion a real big chance.

Elanga latches onto Hall’s pass, gets in behind Spurs’ defence and beats Kinsky to the ball. However, it was a difficult pass to control and his touch is too heavy, causing the opportunity to disappear. Newcastle are certainly looking more adventurous at the start of this second half.

The visitors make a rare foray forward as Hall bends an ambitious curler from long range that flies off target. That is more encouraging for Newcastle.

Early drama at the start of this half as Spurs appeal for a penalty. Thiaw and Marmoush challenge for a 50-50. The Tottenham forward crashes to the floor as the Newcastle captain goes for the clearance. The referee’s on-field decision is no penalty and VAR agrees. After seeing the replays, there wasn’t too much contact and it would have been a harsh penalty if given.

We are back under way for the second half. Will we see a goal at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this evening?

Spurs have been knocking on the door and looked like the far more threatening side, but they’ve been unable to find an opening goal. Newcastle have defended diligently and frustrated their opponents. However, in forward areas, they look disjointed and are lacking serious firepower.

⏸️ @SpursOfficial 0-0 @NUFC There's nothing to separate the two sides at half-time pic.twitter.com/ICFqQ3eXMO

Tel has drifted out to the right wing and turns inside of Nico before whipping a ball into the box which narrowly evades Marmoush. Tonali then bursts forward and passes to Porro, but Hall thwarts Spurs’ latest attack by blocking the makeshift winger’s shot.

I would be worried if I were Matthias Jaissle. Newcastle have not looked comfortable dealing with Tottenham’s corners and goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek has made a couple of good saves this half to keep the scores level.

Much of Newcastle’s attacking play has been aimless, with long diagonal balls pumped forward that the Tottenham defence is prepared for and has tended to deal with easily.

Very little is happening in midfield and neither Joe Willock in the number 10 role nor Yoane Wissa at centre forward has had any real joy in the final third.

It all looks a bit predictable going forward and, if we are being ultra critical, a bit aimless too. They have not forced a save from the Spurs goalkeeper as we approach half time.

Marmoush has become far more involved over the last ten minutes and has showcased his quality with a few notable touches and darting runs. Nevertheless, Spurs have been unable to breach Newcastle’s stubborn defence.

A free-flowing Tottenham move involving Van Hecke and Marmoush ends with Porro sliding a low cross in towards the unmarked Tel at the back post. The Spaniard doesn’t quite can’t enough power on the delivery and Hornicek rushes out to collect.

Marmoush slips a clever pass through to Robertson, who fires in a first-time cross which flies out for a corner. Fernandes whips a corner into the box and Van Hecke wins the header, beating two Newcastle players to the ball. But Hornicek is there to parry the Dutchman’s close-range header away.

Robertson’s deep corner finds an unmarked Marmoush at the back stick. He takes a first-time shot, but his volley bounces wide of the near post. From that range, he needs to be getting that on target.

Marmoush has been on the periphery so far today. Spurs have looked threatening but they could be more attentive with possession at times, especially in midfield.

Van de Ven makes a crucial challenge to stop Wissa from fashioning a shooting opportunity inside the six-yard box after good build-up play from Nico and Elanga.

Newcastle are trying to get the ball forward quickly in this new “vertical” style of Matthias Jaissle but all it is doing at the moment is give it straight back to Tottenham Hotspur.

It has not been a fun first 20 minutes to watch from the visitors who have had little joy breaking through the lines and have invited pressure from Spurs.

The less said about their set piece delivery the better. Harvey Barnes has taken over corner duties from Bruno Guimaraes and has not managed to clear the first Tottenham defender yet.

Tottenham play a short corner and Botman’s headed clearance only finds Porro, who is lurking on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. Porro’s catches the ball on the volley, but his strike flies over. The World Cup winner is playing with real confidence.

Jan Paul van Hecke has played a couple of exceptional forward passes in the early exchanges here. The £52m signing is already demonstrating his ability to start attacks from deep.

The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium screams for a free kick as Porro believes he was brought down by Willock on the edge of the penalty area. There’s minimal contact and referee Peter Bankes is not interested, waving play on.

Tottenham stream into Newcastle’s penalty area, and Tonali’s miscued makes it way through to Porro. He feints to send Miley flying, but Hall is there to make a goal-saving block and thwart Porro’s attempt. Spurs are beginning to grow into this contest and are currently in the ascendency.

Tel forces a flying save from Hornicek! Van Hecke picks out Marmoush with a piercing pass through Newcastle’s midfield, allowing the former Manchester Ciy man to tee up Tel. The winger takes the ball in his stride, cuts inside and whips a venomous effort at goal. Hornicek is up to the task and dives to make the stop.

Tonali has made an unsettled start to this game. He’s already given possession away on a couple of occasions and left space for Newcastle to exploit.

Nico then receives a yellow card on his Newcastle debut for apprehending Gray to stop Tottenham from counter-attacking.

Tonali and Tel give away the ball, allowing Newcastle to attack. Wissa cushions Dedic’s cross with an exquisite touch for Barnes, but the winger curls his effort comfortably off target and fails to trouble Kinsky.

Marmoush has been deployed as the central striker on his Tottenham debut, with Fernandes just behind him as the most advanced midfielder. Porro also looks to be starting on the right wing. It’s a very new-look frontline for Spurs following last weekend’s defeat to Brentford.

Sandro Tonali’s first meaningful action: badly underhitting a simple pass to Micky van de Ven. It resulted in the Spurs captain picking up a yellow card. The Newcastle fans are singing a song about Tonali in the away end, but I won’t repeat the lyrics here.

Tonali under-hits a pass back to Van de Ven, who flies in with a late challenge on Wissa, needlessly colliding with the Newcastle forward. The Spurs captain picks up an early booking. That it not the start he would have wanted.

Newcastle threaten straight away as Elanga nearly lifts an audacious lob over Kinsky from a tight angle. It doesn’t quite squeeze into the bottom corner and Spurs get back to concede a corner inside the first minute. Fernandes then bumps into Dedic off the ball, giving the visitors a free kick.

We are under way in North London. Can either side record their first Premier League win of the season after midweek Carabao Cup victories?

Captains Van de Ven and Thiaw lead their respective sides out onto the pitch. The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is in full voice, with kick-off just minutes away.

"Quality." 🤷‍♂️Matthias Jaissle on what Nico González adds to the Newcastle side 💬 pic.twitter.com/yjMBcr0pUm

It is not the sight of their former player Sandro Tonali in a Tottenham Hotspur shirt that will worry Newcastle United.

Omar Marmoush was only at Manchester City for 18 months but managed to score seven goals in just five appearances against Newcastle, including a hat-trick back in February 2025.

The Egyptian has moved to Spurs seeking regular first team football and will go up against the team he has enjoyed facing more than any other in English football.

Newcastle, of course, have a new manager Matthias Jaissle and are playing a different style of football under the German. Despite an unbeaten start in league and cup, the defence has not looked particularly assured.

That could make the ideal opponents for Spurs as they look to prove last season’s miserable home form is not going to continue into this one.

I’m fascinated to see how Newcastle play here. They were happy to sit back, soak up pressure and go direct in attack, mainly on the counter. That sort of approach could be even more effective away from home than at St James’ Park.

For me, it is far too early to say a summer of change has worked for Newcastle. We will have a better idea after this game.

Sandro Tonali’s departure from Newcastle United did not provoke the same extreme anger as Alexander Isak’s acrimonious move to Liverpool or the sadness of captain Bruno Guimarães’ switch to Arsenal. That is largely because nobody will miss him as much.

There is no doubt the Italy international’s determination to leave for Tottenham Hotspur did rankle supporters, especially given the club had stood by him during a 10-month betting ban, but Tonali was only a good player for Newcastle, not a great one.

Unsurprisingly, Roberto De Zerbi has made five changes to the team that wilted against Brentford.

Marcos Senesi, Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher, Mikey Moore and Richarlison have been dropped. In come Micky van de Ven, who captains the side, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pedro Porro, Mateus Fernandes and Omar Marmoush. Savinho is missing altogether.

Good evening from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there is no sign of new Spurs winger Savio. After his thrilling debut against Charlton Athletic in midweek, the £75m forward seems to have picked up an injury. We’ll learn the reason for his absence very soon.

As expected, Sandro Tonali starts in the Spurs midfield. His second Premier League game for his new club comes against his former team. There’s also a start for new man Omar Marmoush, who is making his first appearance for Spurs following his move from City.

Our Spurs side to face Newcastle! 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/djFKnl6nsi

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

Nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

Newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his new surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

Despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in new boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

Newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

#1943. Senior Cup exit is a setback for Bognor Regis Town – but bigger picture looks rosy

Danny Hollands’ side went out after a 3-2 reverse to the SCFL outfit, meaning the Rocks are now out of all the cup competitions.

The loss came on the back of a 2-1 derby day victory over Littlehampton Town in the Isthmian South Central division on Saturday. And the Nye Camp aces get the chance to improve their points tally on Saturday when they host Hayes & Yeading.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The victory – after two reverses on the spin -- against the lowly Sportsfield outfit maintained the club’s spot in third in the league standings, with Egham Town top and Jersey Bulls, who the Rocks visit next week, second.

Another positive to come out of that game was the full return of striker Cal Laycock after a long lay-off -- and similarly against United a bonus was the goal-scoring return of long-term absentee Billy Allcock.

It was assistant manager Ben Kneller who spoke to the club’s YouTube channel about the cup exit to Eastbourne, against whom youngsters such as Dennis Wooldridge, Noah Light, Toby Kingswell, Archie Bennett and Louie Williams all featured -- and some of those had actually played the night before in an U18s game, too.

Kneller said: “We need to keep moving forward but all in all, if we were stood here having the conversation last year when we first game (to manage) and we said, 'listen, we are going to be third or fourth in the league come mid-November, we have lost two games in 26, but you're out of the cups, would you have taken it? You probably would have done. We need to step back to see where we are, (compared) to where we were.

"It was a little bit of real reality check after Saturday when we had 1,300 in (and beat our local rivals). We are not happy to be out and not happy with a few in the dressing room – but there are positives within the negatives.

"Noah is a very intelligent footballer (for instance). They (some u18s) train with us on a Thursday and they are around the environment all the time and just because they don't feature in games they are still in around along with others.

“We want to progress young players in the area and that is what Bognor is all about. It's not all about winning this and winning that, it is very much about building from the base and we believe in that. From our side of things there is a pathway for the 18s and we have shown it."

On being out of all the cups, he added: "We would like to have a cup run but you can never guarantee it but we would have liked to deliver it Maybe we strip the squad back a little more now we are out of the cups and we realign."

Here’s Liam Goodley’s full report from the Senior Cup defeat

Bognor were knocked out of the Sussex Senior Cup under the lights at Nyewood Lane as their makeshift side were put to the test by well organised, Eastbourne United.

Tommy Block went into the book early on for his challenge after a back pass. Rhyle Overden crossed it in from the free-kick but straight into the arms of Archie Bennett in the Bognor goal.

Charlie Gunson latched on to a loose ball after a long ball into the area and his strike was deflected away from the back legs of a defender on 11 minutes. Archie Bennett did well to stop two players twice after James Hull's cross that was hit low into the box on 15 minutes, keeping the scoreline goalless.

Gunson did well to wind into the box but his shot was deflected into the path of Ollie Lovell who was also denied by an Eastbourne body. Joe Overy did well on the attack for the visitors. He cut inside after some swift passing play but fired it over the crossbar from outside the area.

Anderson hooked the ball high into the area from the freekick. Block was unmarked as he leapt up to head that towards goal. The ball looped up kindly for the goalkeeper though.

Sorge Nones did all the hard work winding his way through the area but blasted over the bar with his left foot on 37 minutes. Secka had to punch away a dipping direct freekick frm Gunson off the left side on 41 minutes. HT 0-0

Changes at half-time saw Block, Benny Read and Gunson come off for Josh Batt, Toby Kingswell and Ethan Robb. Batt got the ball forward to Louie Williams, but after rounding his marker he fired it low and into the grateful arms of Secka from a tight angle on 54 minutes.

Bognor made another change on 60 minutes that saw Maadhav Jagota replaced by Callum Laycock and Lovell came off for Billy Allcock.

A swift move down the left saw Eastbourne United take the lead on 67 minutes. Overy used his pace to run down the left before diverting a low ball into the area and ex-Rock Callum Barlow knocked it in from close range.

Williams set Kingswell on his way down the right wing but Kingswell smacked his cross out of play for a goal kick in a poor half for Bognor.

Robb's free-kick curled dangerously into the area on 78 minutes. The ball was knocked down wide of the right post as the goalkeeper watched it roll past the right post.

James Stone, off the bench, did really well to compose himself running in front of defence before powerfully driving the ball into the net beyond a diving Bennett on 79 minutes, extending United's lead.

Harvey Whyte put in a great delivery from the right and Laycock got their ahead of his marker to get something onto it, and managed to divert the ball low, of which Secka managed to save low to his right.

Another forward ball saw Billy Allcock run through and his first strike was blocked before he followed up to net it on the rebound on 84 minutes for 2-1.

However, that reduced lead didn't last long as Stone worked hard on the right before putting it on a plate for Overy to knock into the net on 85 minutes.

Bognor got another goal back direct from Robb's corner as Laycock netted it with his head on 91 minutes. Bognor were attacking towards the end for a last gasp equaliser but Eastbourne United were good defensively to stave off the danger late on.

So the Rocks were knocked out of the Sussex Senior Cup at the third round stage and are now able to fully focus on their league campaign with some massive games coming up, including next up, a home tie against Hayes & Yeading United this Saturday (21st November, 3pm).

Rocks: Bennett, Read, Wooldridge, Anderson, Whyte, Block, Jagota, Lovell, Williams, Gunson, Light. Subs (all used): Batt, Laycock, Allcock, Robb, Kingswell.

#1942. England deliver the spectacular as Three Lions strip world champions Spain of their invincibility and give Thomas Tuchel the proof that his coaching IS working, writes OLIVER HOLT

Published: 17:02 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 04:59 EST, 16 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel had said he wanted evidence. He needed to believe his coaching was working. He needed to see something that told him he could help England overcome those DNA deficiencies he had identified in the aftermath of the devastating World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

He needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best. He needed to cling on to the idea that they could overhaul Spain, that the work he was doing could improve England so much they could win the European Championship in 2028 and end this country’s cursed cycle of despair.

Proof of concept, he called it on Saturday night when England arrived in Madrid. ‘This will be proof of concept on the highest level,’ Tuchel predicted. ‘It's the biggest test in world football. Spain seems unbeatable but we are trying to take it away from them. We are up for something spectacular.’

Something spectacular is what Tuchel promised and something spectacular is what both he and England delivered. Spain had not lost for 43 matches, a world record, but number 44 was beyond them. For just over an hour, England destroyed them. They outplayed them. They stripped them of their invincibility.

And then, when Elliot Anderson was sent off after 63 minutes for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Spain stormed back into the game, England somehow managed to hold on for a momentous victory in the screaming, yelling cauldron of the Metropolitano. This was proof alright. This was proof positive.

Sure, it was nervy for half an hour. And, yes, England nearly found a way to throw it away. But the way they played when it was 11 v 11 was enough for any England fan to believe that England under Tuchel can climb back to the summit of a major tournament and gaze down on a view they have not seen for 60 years.

England recorded a famous victory over Spain in Madrid as they won a five-goal thriller

Elliot Anderson's red card opened the door for the world champions to mount a comeback

James Trafford made a superb double save in stoppage time to preserve England's lead

Yes, this was a Nations League dead rubber because both teams were already guaranteed progress to the quarter-finals next March, but there was no mistaking its wider significance. This was proof England are good enough to turn away from the trail of tears that has been their path for so long. Before the game, Spain had held the World Cup aloft again as one final reminder of England’s failure but by the end, by the time goalkeeper James Trafford had added to the drama with a miraculous double save, the glory and the 3-2 triumph was England’s.

Spain had won their last 12 matches in succession and the sport’s last two major tournament. They had not been beaten since March 2024 and had not lost at home since September 2022. England ended that run with 10 men. What a night. It was a special kind of crazy.

England had celebrated Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph and caps record at Wembley last week but Spain took things a stage further before the game. The boys who won the U15 World Cup were introduced to the crowd. Then the World Cup itself was carried on for goalkeeper Unai Simon to hold aloft.

England ignored it all. They started the game like an express train. They nearly took the lead inside the first two minutes when Jude Bellingham met a corner from Declan Rice on the edge of the six-yard-box and was only denied by a brilliant reaction save from Simon. Gordon’s follow-up was destined for the bottom corner before it was blocked by a Spain defender.

Spain were rattled. The crowd whistled. England forced their opponents into mistake after mistake at the back. From one of those successful presses, Kane drilled a shot inches wide. Gordon, who has made such a fine start to his Barcelona career, revelled on the stage and caused right back Marc Pubill all manner of anxieties.

Spain could barely break out of their own half but when they did, after a quarter of an hour, Yamal ran at Lewis Hall and nutmegged him before Rice chopped the teenager down. Rice was booked by French referee Clement Turpin and Lamal windmilled his hands in the air to wind up the crowd.

Pubill was replaced midway through the half. It looked like an injury but it could have been hurt pride or twisted blood. Gordon had barely given him a moment’s rest. In fact, Gordon was tireless. He harried Martin Zubimendi off the ball with ease and almost set up a chance for Bellingham.

England got the goal they deserved a minute before half-time. The build-up was controversial. Anderson played a fine through ball to Kane that doubled as a crunching tackle on Marc Cucurella. Cucurella went down as if he had been shot, which is what Cucurella always does.

Ben White slotted the ball through the keeper's legs after a brilliant England move

Harry Kane celebrates goal No 93 for England after giving them the lead from the penalty spot

The referee allowed play to continue. Kane advanced on goal and turned inside Pau Cubarsi, Spain’s brilliant young defender. Cubarsi brought him down and the referee pointed to the spot. Cucurella still lay prone. Bellingham, his Real Madrid teammate, leaned over him and told him what he thought of him.

There were a whole host of VAR checks but England passed all of them. The crowd whistled their distaste. Kane missed a penalty in the Wembley game between these two teams in September but he did not miss this one. Simon guessed the right way but Kane hit it too fiercely and it bulged the back of the net. It was his 93rd goal for England.

Spain are not used to being bossed around like this. Tempers flared after the whistle blew for half-time. Ben White and Fabian Ruiz joined in a disagreement of some sort and soon there was a flurry of pushing and shoving. It stopped short of being a melee but it was obvious Spain were shaken.

Eight minutes into the second half, England went further ahead. Rice swung a corner into the centre of the box and, as the usual wrestling match unfolded, Ezri Konsa ran in gloriously unmarked and nodded the ball down and past the helpless Simon from close range.

Four minutes later, against a general backdrop of disbelief, England were three ahead. What a goal it was, too. Bellingham, who had been his usual superhuman self, muscled his way free in the centre and fed the ball out to Kane.

Kane held the ball up and played it back to Bellingham on the edge of the box. Bellingham spotted the overlapping run of White and found him with a clever pass. White took a touch and slotted the ball past Simon. It was the Arsenal full-back’s first competitive England start, too. Maybe now England fans will stop booing him.

This was the night Thomas Tuchel had been crying out for as he got the evidence he demanded

Ezri Konsa met Declan Rice's set-piece to plant an unstoppable header in the back of the net

But then, midway through the half, England gave Spain a lifeline. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession by Yamal and as Yamal bore down on goal, Anderson pulled him back. Anderson was shown a red card and Spain were awarded a penalty. Oyarzabal waited for Trafford to commit himself and then stroked the ball into the opposite corner.

The atmosphere in the stadium was transformed. Spain sensed vulnerability in England for the first time. Fifteen minutes from time, they pulled another goal back. Yamal sprinted away down the right and slid the ball into the middle for substitute Nico Williams, who sidefooted it past Trafford.

Now, it was like the Alamo. Yamal tormented England. Trafford dived at full length to push away one of his shots and then got down at his near post to divert a shot that was creeping in. White produced another of the moments of the night with a flying block to keep out a goalbound shot from Williams.

Spain threw everything at England but England would not yield. When Trafford made that double save, everyone knew. It was to be England’s night. Tuchel had his proof of concept.

#1941. Liverpool transfer news: £21m Lamine Camara 'confirmed' to be on radar as Andoni Iraola faces major midfield problem

By Lewis Nolan | 18 Nov 2026 02:09

Liverpool want to sign Athletic Club midfielder Mikel Jauregizar, who is seen as an alternative to Lamine Camara, the newest report has claimed.

The Merseysiders are preparing to take on rivals Manchester United on Sunday, and victory will be key for the club's pursuit of a place in Premier League's top four.

If Andoni Iraola's side are to get the better of the Red Devils, they will need to win the midfield battle, though that has been an area of concern for some time.

Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai have often disappointed in the middle of the pitch, and that has led to calls for reinforcements.

While Liverpool have strongly been credited interest in Monaco star Camara, Anfield Watch have now claimed that the Reds also have Athletic Bilbao's Jauregizar on their list of targets.

Valued at just under £21m by Transfermarkt, Jauregizar would likely not command as high a fee as Camara, which would make a January move more realistic.

The 23-year-old has only started three La Liga games this season, featuring in seven, and he has won 51% of his duels in the top flight.

Jauregizar only won 47% of his duels in the league in 2025-26, but his struggles in that regard are not shared with Camara, who has won 66% of his duels this campaign in Ligue 1.

The Monaco midfielder is also more accomplished with the ball, and he should still be seen as the premium option, either in January or the summer.

Trey Nyoni will almost certainly become a starter in the next few years, and signing another midfielder would pose a problem in terms of guaranteeing playing time.

Szoboszlai and Gravenberch are contracted to Anfield until 2031 and 2032 respectively, so moving on either player would be difficult.

Alexis Mac Allister has been the Reds' best midfielder this season and has arguably been among the best performers in that role across the division, so losing him in the coming summer would weaken the squad.

Liverpool may soon be faced with a painful decision, with at least one of their established stars likely to head for the exit doors in the coming months.

#1939. Broadbridge Heath hit Haywards Heath for six to reach Sussex Senior Cup quarter-finals

Ben Royall (2), Ollie Rawlins (2), Zac Young and Charlie Connell scored to put Chris Simmons’ side into the quarter-finals.

Simmons said: “It was a great result for us in what could have been a really tricky game. They are a very good side and ready to push on to step four but they didn’t take the early chances they had and we were really clinical.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

“They should have been a goal in front from a mistake by us, then within 30 seconds we were 1-0 up.

“The wet/sticky surface made it difficult for both sides who looked to play but overall I think the neutrals got their money’s worth.

“It was nice to make five changes from Saturday, get minutes into lads returning from injury and reach the quarter-finals.

“The league is our priority but everyone loves a cup run.”

It completed a perfect week for the Bears after Saturday’s 2-0 Isthmian South East win at Margate, in which Luke Bejashvili scored both. Heath host Hastings on Saturday.

Here is Andrew Crisp’s Heath v Heath match report…

On paper this midweek trip to Southern Combination League leaders Haywards Heath Town looked a potential banana skin for Chris Simmons’ Broadbridge Heath.

The hosts may be a division below the Bears but they have made a great start to the season, five points clear at the top of the Premier Division, unbeaten at home after ten matches and having knocked cup favourites Brighton & Hove Albion out by 2-0 in an earlier round, but things don’t always work out as some may predict.

Simmons made five changes to the starting line-up that won 2-0 at Margate three days earlier, four at the back including Bailey Cotton on his way back from injury and making his first start since September and Ollie Rawlins making just his second start of the season after injury.

Broadbridge Heath got off to a great start on 3 minutes when Ben Holden received the ball on the halfway line and drove forward into the Haywards Heath half before playing the ball out wide to Ben Royall advancing down the left, and the Bears full-back cut inside and struck a low right foot shot from distance into the bottom right corner of the net.

The Bears doubled their lead on 24 minutes with Holden and Royal involved again: this time Holden, in the centre of the park, played the ball into the feet of Royall with his back to goal and closely marked, the Bears defender turned his marker and ran towards the Haywards Heath penalty area before striking a low left foot shot across the goal into the far corner.

At the other end Jack Barnes powered a header from a corner onto the top of the crossbar and Bears skipper Brad Peters reacted quickly to clear the ball off the goal-line but it was Broadbridge Heath who increased their lead on 32 minutes.

An interchange of passes ended with Luke Bejashvili playing the ball into the feet of Holden who played a first time pass to Ollie Rawlins some 25 yards out and with his back to goal and the Heath striker turned sharply to power a right foot shot into the bottom right corner giving the hosts’ keeper Charlie Roberts no chance of stopping.

Minutes later Broadbridge Heath’s Sal Marino played a defence-splitting ball to send Charlie Connell through on goal but Roberts was off his line quickly to force the player wide of goal and instead Connell played the ball back into the path of Rawlins on the edge of the “D” who blasted his shot high and wide.

A minute before the break the hosts pulled a goal back when Josh Wright crossed the ball from the right flank into the Broadbridge Heath penalty area where the ball bobbled around the six yard box before falling kindly to Charlie Meehan to tap in from close range.

Broadbridge Heath restored their three goal advantage almost immediately when a long ball was played down the left channel and chased down by Rawlins who delivered a left foot cross into the path of Zac Young, who hit a sweet left foot shot from 12 yards which was saved brilliantly by Roberts. Young pounced on the loose ball and was brought down by a clumsy challenge, and the match referee immediately pointed to the penalty spot with nobody from Haywards Heath questioning the decision and Young got up to convert the spot kick for his sixth goal of the season to make it 1-4 at the break.

Haywards Heath needed an early second half goal to get back into the game but the reverse happened 2 minutes into the restart when Broadbridge Heath goalkeeper Stan Williamson intercepted a right wing cross and threw the ball out quickly to Young in the centre of the park. He drove forward to the halfway line before playing the ball wide right to Charlie Connell, who took the ball towards the goal-line and then delivered a right wing pass across the goal to Rawlins to score from six yards.

Heath added a sixth goal on the hour mark when Rawlins received the ball wide on the right and played a long ball towards the far post where it was headed in by Connell from 8 yards to near enough secure the win for the Bears.

Simmons was able to swap his players around which included the welcome return to the side for Mason Doughty, the Heath striker with eight goals from 13 games this season has missed the last eight games through injury.

Haywards Heath added a second in time added-on when a combination of Wright and Barnes won the ball off a Bears defender and linked up well down the right channel before the ball was played inside to Barnes who finished with aplomb.

BBH: Williamson, Cotton (Thiselton 60), Royall, Marino, Peters, Salaam (Richardson 65), Bejashvili, Holden, Rawlins (Doughty 70), Connell (Hards 61), Young.

#1936. Arsenal transfer news: David Ornstein drops interesting update on Eli Junior Kroupi ahead of January

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 06:57

Arsenal could face imminent disappointment in their pursuit of AFC Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, with David Ornstein providing an update on the 19-year-old's future.

The Gunners have been monitoring the Frenchman after his impressive performances, but a move for him in the January transfer window is now looking increasingly unlikely.

Ornstein has also suggested that Kroupi could favour a move away from the Premier League when he eventually leaves the Vitality Stadium.

In a recent The Athletic Q&A, Ornstein downplayed the prospect of the Cherries sanctioning a January departure, saying the club has little financial incentive to sell midway through the campaign.

The forward is under contract until 2030, meaning the Cherries are in a strong negotiating position and can afford to wait until the summer before considering significant offers.

Ornstein also highlighted that Kroupi only made his first appearance of the season on October 25th after an injury lay-off, with Bournemouth keen to benefit from his contributions during the remainder of the campaign.

Perhaps more significantly for Arsenal, the ever-reliable journalist suggested that the teenager could prefer a move abroad rather than another Premier League club.

Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona have both been heavily linked, with Ornstein indicating that the information available to him points towards those destinations being more likely than a move within England.

He did acknowledge that an exceptional financial offer from a Premier League club could change the situation, but his expectation is that Bournemouth would be more receptive to a sale next summer.

Ornstein's update represents a significant complication for Arsenal, who could now need to explore alternative attacking targets if they want to strengthen in January.

Kroupi's contract situation means Bournemouth have little reason to entertain offers, while the player's reported preference for moving abroad further weakens the Gunners' position.

Antonio Nusa could therefore become a more realistic alternative for Gunners boss Mikel Arteta.

The RB Leipzig winger is another young attacking talent attracting Premier League interest, with Arsenal previously linked alongside Tottenham and reportedly confident of competing for his signature.

Nusa would not necessarily provide the same centre-forward option as Kroupi, but his ability to operate out wide could address another area where Arsenal need greater depth.

Ultimately, Kroupi remains an exciting long-term target, but the combination of Bournemouth's stance and his apparent preference for a move abroad suggests Arsenal may have to be patient or turn their attention elsewhere in January.

Former Rangers and Sunderland head coach Michael Beale has broken his silence on his turbulent 177-day spell in charge of Belgian Pro League side Zulte Waregem after resigning last week.

Beale, 46, brought down the curtain on his short time at the Elindus Arena following the 4-1 defeat to Sint-Truidense last week, which made it six consecutive league defeats. Their worst run of results since October 7, 2018, they are just four points above the relegation zone.

His spell in Belgium was plagued by rumours of a breakdown in his relationship with senior figures at the club over Waregem’s direction and strategy. Beale actually started the campaign brightly, going unbeaten in their opening five games. However, their form quickly deteriorated, and they have failed to register a victory since September 6.

His first managerial role since being sacked after just 12 games in charge at Sunderland almost three years ago, he exited Waregem with an identical record to the one he held at the Stadium of Light, with four wins, two draws, and six losses, meaning he left both sides with a 33.3% win rate after 12 games.

In a short statement confirming his departure, Waregem said: “After several internal discussions between the head coach and the club, both parties decided to end their collaboration by mutual agreement.” Zulte Waregem are yet to appoint Beale’s permanent successor, with interim head coach Steve Colpaert expected to take charge of their league game vs Royal Antwerp at the weekend.

A week on from his departure, Beale penned an emotional farewell message to Waregem via his official Instagram page, writing: “Waregem, thankyou. I will never forget the welcome you gave me and I have been overwhelmed by all your messages and kind words over the last few days.

“This community has become a home to me and to everyone I met in the local shops, coffee houses, parks, restaurants and bars: thank you. Many of you have become true friends and you have made me feel completely one of your own. I also want to show my gratitude to the players and staff for their hard work, dedication and the special memories we created together. You have been a pleasure to work with and I wish you every success in the future.”

The ex-Rangers manager first joined Rangers as first-team coach during Steven Gerrard’s spell as manager at Ibrox. However, he left to join the former Liverpool icon in a similar role when he was appointed at Aston Villa in November 2021. Shortly afterwards, Beale took on his first managerial role with Queens Park Rangers.

He lasted just six months at Loftus Road before being poached by Rangers as a replacement for Giovanni van Bronckhorst. He struggled in the main role at Rangers, though, and was sacked in October 2023 before joining Sunderland three months later.

#1933. Derek McInnes issues stern Rangers transfer warning as Ibrox boss sends key message to possible winter suitors

Derek McInnes has stressed that Rangers have no intention of selling their key players in January as he looks to maintain the club’s growing momentum ahead of Saturday night’s Premiership clash with Motherwell.

The Ibrox boss believes retaining the core of his squad will be vital to Rangers’ silverware ambitions this season, insisting that the club has no desire to part with regular starters despite potential interest from elsewhere.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

While conceding that an offer too good to turn down would have to be considered, McInnes emphasised that Rangers are keen to avoid disruption to the squad when the winter transfer window opens.

“We will be keeping them,” he declared emphatically. “We're not looking to move players out, certainly players who have been playing regularly. We want to shut that down really early. We know and understand that keeping that core of players and having that stability is so important for us.”

Rangers return to league action against a Motherwell side McInnes claims is beginning to rediscover the qualities that made them such a formidable opponent last season under Jens Berthel Askou.

They head to Fir Park aiming to extend their 12-game unbeaten run, but McInnes anticipates a difficult test against a Motherwell side that has shown signs of improvement under Alfred Johansson’s care in recent weeks.

“I think they've started to look a wee bit more like that team that got a lot of success last year,” McInnes admitted. “They've got a lot of traits and similarities. They've lost two or three key players, but they still have the nucleus of that team and you can see they've got a clear idea of what they're trying to do.

“The difficulty when you go away from home is obvious. You've got to make sure you do so much right. It's not just about being good technically. You've got to make sure that all the other facets are there, that you need to compete right from the outset.”

McInnes highlighted Rangers’ recent away win at St Mirren as a blueprint for Saturday’s encounter, adding: “Something similar will be required. If we want to get to where we want to get to this season, it's a game that presents us with three points. And we want to make sure we leave Motherwell with all three, if we can.”

Rangers have kept eight clean sheets during their near two-month unbeaten run, with McInnes eager for his side to maintain their defensive solidity as they enter a demanding run of fixtures.

“I don't like it when we're too comfortable," he explained. “If we're four or five up and we’re deep into the second half, then I'll be all fine. But when the game is still in the balance, particularly away from home, and you're 1-0 up or 2-0 up, there's still work to do.

“We should be proud of that [clean sheets], but I thought we put it at risk a wee bit once or twice against St Mirren and I think it was unnecessary. We've got to make sure that we don't get complacent with what we're doing and we stay on top of the job."

With three consecutive home fixtures following Saturday's trip to North Lanarkshire, Rangers have an opportunity to build further momentum. McInnes, however, knows the immediate priority is on overcoming a rejuvenated Motherwell side.

“We're not expecting it to be straightforward,” he stated. “But I do expect us to bring a strong performance if we're going to win the game. I think everybody, certainly me and the staff, and I'm sure the supporters are the same, are starting to see a team that we think we can get behind and get a bit of confidence from.”

There was positive news on the injury front following the international break, with Daisuke Yokota returning to training earlier this week alongside Ross McCrorie, while Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin are continuing their rehabilitation through increased work on the grass.

#1932. Eastbourne United fans find another win to talk about for years to come

For Eastbourne United it has to be between THAT FA Vase semi-final, beating Crawley Town in the Sussex Senior Cup, or, on the other side of that coin, the following Senior Cup game, where Bognor put seven past Simon Rowland’s men.

Spool forward 12 years, and United had a chance at restoring their good name in West Sussex, again in the Senior Cup.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After a deluge on the way to the game, the United faithful were pleasantly surprised to see a pleasant evening for this step 4 v step 5 encounter.

As the referee got the match underway, it became immediately obvious that Anthony Storey’s boys were giving no quarter at all to the higher league team – Joe Overy running head down at the defence time and again as Charlie Ball, Callum Barlow and James Hull all went close top opening the scoring, with no real penetration from Bognor until the 20th minute, when Zach Robitaille and Dan Hull combined to clear off the line.

On the half hour, Overy decided to go it alone, his shot going just over the bar. Jorge Nones was looking very lively indeed and was unfortunate not to score, the Bognor keeper again earning his corn with a point blank save.

As the teams went in 0-0 at half time, nerves were showing among the Bognor crowd – maybe the lower league team will run out of steam?

Had they done their homework, they would know that Eastbourne United are one of the fittest teams in the SCFL Premier, and so it was that as the teams came out for the second half, if anything United had stepped their game up.

James Hull had picked up a nasty cut in the first half and was replaced by the lively Freddie Jones on the hour. Almost straight away, Overy crossed for Barlow who made no mistake against his old club, to the absolute horror of the home support.

Bognor made a triple change in response, but to be honest did not really look to have an answer. James Stone replaced Barlow a few minutes later, and within minutes Ball broke down the right, his cross finding Stone for a great finish and 2-0. The upset was definitely on the cards.

Alieu Secka saved well from Cal Laycock, but with 5 minutes to go, the lifeline appeared and it was 2-1. United were not rattled – quite the opposite as Jones went straight up the other end and crossed for Overy to make it 3-1.

Alfie Gander replaced Ball as the game moved to 6 minutes of added time. Right at the end Bognor snuck a second goal, but it was too late, it made for an exciting last couple of minutes, but everyone knew that the game was up, indeed as the referee blew the final whistle there was generous applause from the Rocks supporters after a game played in a very good atmosphere.

Eastbourne United are in the quarter-finals and ready for another adventure in the next round.

On Saturday Guernsey are the visitors to the Oval for a 2pm kick-off, another match that will be vital in United’s promotion push.

Eastbourne Town’s Senior Cup interest is over. Sonny Walsh’s goal wasn’t enough to prevent a 2-1 defeat to Lewes at The Saffrons, also on Tuesday night.

But there was better news for Jude Macdonald’s team in the Isthmian South East last Saturday – they drew 1-1 at Sheppey, with Alfie Rogers their scorer. That ended a run of eight league defeats on the trot for Town and took them off bottom spot, now occupied by Horley.

Macdonald’s men host Whitstable tomorrow.

#1931. Celtic ‘disaster’ fuels Hearts trophy quest as Jambos’ Mr Versatile names ex-Liverpool hero inspiring dream

Hearts’ versatile attacker Rogers Mato says the Tynecastle dressing room is determined to end the club’s 14-year wait for a major trophy after seeing the title slip through their fingers in the final minutes of last season.

Mato, 23, played just three league games for Hearts after arriving on an initial loan from North Macedonian outfit FK Vardar last January, but has featured regularly for the Gorgie side this season after making his move permanent in the summer by penning a three-year contract in July.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Originally signed as a wide forward, the Ugandan international was deployed as a left-back against Turkish outfit Trabzonspor in the Europa League earlier this month, with Hearts’ injury crisis seeing Mato pitted against former Liverpool icon, Mo Salah. However, he admits it’s another ex-Anfield hero, Senegal international Sadio Mane, that he takes inspiration from as he looks ahead to the African Cup of Nations in his homeland next summer.

“I grew up just watching the other players on TV and sneaking in the stadiums,” Mato told RG. “I didn't even have a chance to be like a ball boy to give them the balls in the national team. I only did that on the club level. But wearing the national team jersey is a big responsibility, we're representing our families, our dream, and millions of Ugandans.

“Mane is my all-time favourite African player. I would love to wear the captain's armband. I would love to lead my country. We grow by responsibilities, not by age. So, that would have a massive impact and would be a massive confidence booster for me to be leading the nation to glory.”

The 23-year-old says he is using the pain of defeat to fuel another of his major dreams - bringing silverware at Tynecastle. Refusing to concede his side are out of the title race this season despite being 11 points behind league leaders Celtic, he admits the crushing way that a first top flight title win since 1960 trophy was ripped from their grasp by two late Hoops goal on the final day last season still stings.

“It's been ups and downs [since joining Hearts],” he admits. “Coming from Macedonia, playing 90-plus minutes and then coming on for Hearts and playing for 13 minutes in three games and 13 minutes in the second half of the season. It's been ups and downs, but with patience, everything will come to an end.

“I just had to come here and wait for my time, but every time we just have to be patient. I needed to work hard on myself, work hard for the team, so I can get more game time. It's all about mentality. You have to adapt to any coach that comes your way. If you don't adapt, you're dead as a footballer. Last season was hectic and brutal for the team, for the fans. Those last minutes [vs Celtic], it was a heartbreak for everyone, for every Hearts fan. It was a total disaster.

“But we're looking forward to give it all this season. But suddenly we got a lot of injuries here and there, but those who are still fit, we're trying our best to still keep [the title race] alive for our friends, our brothers who are injured, so they can come and join us [when they're back]. Because we can't let it down, we still have to keep the hopes for the first place."

#1930. Crawley Town chief has his say on whether 3pm football blackout is still relevant

The Premier League and EFL are set to hold serious conversations about the blackout’s future next year with pretty much every TV slot now exhausted.

Removing the blackout – which is a rule that prevents live football matches from being broadcast on television or streaming services between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays – could have a detrimental effect on attendances and finances, especially clubs in the lower tiers like Crawley Town.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The blackout is under threat and television rights deals for the Premier League, EFL and Scottish Premiership are all up for renewal in 2029-30 and last year, Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said there were no plans to remove the blackout – introduced in 2003 by UEFA as Article 48.

But this summer there appeared to be a shift in emphasis, with Masters saying there would be talks with the EFL ahead of the renewal of TV rights. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has urged caution and suggested the health of the football pyramid should come first.

The only leagues that apply Article 48 are England, Scotland and Northern Ireland. No other major country qualifies for the blackout - it is a tradition that is unique to football in the United Kingdom.

CEO Allman gave his personal opinion – and not necessarily that of the club – about the situation and what it would mean if it ended.

He said: “My personal opinion is that the 3pm blackout currently works well in protecting the current football pyramid. I hear the arguments about it not being in place in other countries, but there is no pyramid like the UK pyramid so am not sure it is a fair comparison.

"We see notable increases in attendances during international breaks as well as drop offs for Tuesday night games for example where they are available on SkySports+ so in general, whilst removing the blackout, would arguably increase the exposure of clubs like Crawley, would levy that with actual attendances dropping off, which whilst having the obvious financial implication, will also have impacts on atmospheres and the general match-day feel.”

So it’s clear whether he would oppose the ending of the blackout? “I wouldn’t be in favour - as I say, I think the pyramid is what stands us apart from other countries and sports, and with that, would encourage fans to go out and experience the full pyramid, rather than looking for more Premier League games on TV.”

He added: “Whilst I understand the argument of increased coverage, I wouldn’t levy that against supporters being in the stadium, buying a pint, eating a burger, cheering their team on and in turn, financially supporting the club to allow us to kick on across the board.”

#1929. Ex-Celtic hero reveals impact of ‘all night’ gaming on former teammate as GTA VI launch comes with warning

Former Celtic winger Aiden McGeady has revealed that a former Parkhead teammate became so addicted to computer games that he was rated as one of the world’s highest-ranked players.

McGeady’s comments arrive on the back of the highly anticipated launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI), which was released on November 19 and is expected to be the best-selling action-adventure video game of all time, having already shattered launch records.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Generating an estimated $1.65 billion across over 17 million pre-order copies before its release, GTA VI is the first release in the franchise from Rockstar Games, which has a flagship development studio based in Edinburgh, in 13 years, and has several celebrity fans that include footballers Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Thibaut Courtois.

"Tommy Gravesen would play Call of Duty when I was at Celtic,” said McGeady. “We had a group, so we'd go home from training and play it. Tommy would never give us his gamertag. I don't know why, but I don't think he wanted us playing with him. But apparently he was like third or fourth in the world at Call of Duty on team deathmatch.

"Somebody managed to get his gamertag and added him and he had 45 days of playing time. 45 days of playing time! You look down the list of your friends and the next one after him was like two days and Tommy had 45 days. So we were like, Tommy must have been going home and just sitting there all day and all night. So yeah, I mean it is addictive isn't it? I have seen it in football before, lads staying up until like three or four in the morning before a game to play Call of Duty and stuff like that. Not ideal, but what are you going to do?"

However, despite the popularity of GTA VI, the 40-year-old doesn’t expect any current professionals to follow in the footsteps Celtic, Everton and Real Madrid. McGeady admits he has seen several players take portable games consoles on the team coach when headed to away games, and the ex-Celtic and Hibs man has warned the younger generation to not follow Gravesen’s example.

“I don't think GTA VI would be a problem because anybody that brings a portable PlayStation or a portable Xbox, they're obsessed with it anyway, aren't they?” McGeady said, speaking to BOYLE Sports. I've been on buses before and it's like lads will get the PlayStations out and it's like FIFA or Call of Duty or it's Fortnite, whatever it is. Lads do that anyway, they're obsessed with it anyway.

"So I don't think GTA VI is going to create a new breed of a new market of players who are just going to start playing PlayStation. I think the people that already play it will play it anyway. I think most footballers are fairly responsible and most Premier League footballers are fairly responsible. I don't think it's going to take over their life. Maybe for the younger players it could be an issue because they can be addicted to these games.”

#1928. Liverpool transfer news: Reds join Barcelona race for Brazilian defender amid Van Dijk doubt

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 07:04

Liverpool have reportedly entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem, with the future of Virgil van Dijk still unresolved. The Dutch defender’s contract runs until the end of the season and he has yet to reach an agreement over an extension, while Liverpool are monitoring the market.

While the January transfer window is yet to open, Liverpool are facing a dilemma behind the scenes. With his contract running until the end of the season, Van Dijk has no renewal agreement in progress and can sign a pre-contract agreement from January.

With the situation of the Dutch defender unresolved, Liverpool have entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem.

According to Sports Illustrated, Liverpool have sent scouts to follow the rise of Arthur Dias closely and are now assessing the possibility of buying him from Athletico Paranaense. The 19-year-old defender is one of the breakout stars of Brazilian football in 2026 and is being watched by several European clubs.

Barcelona’s interest in Arthur Dias is long-standing, as being left-footed and comfortable playing out from the back are qualities missing from manager Hansi Flick’s squad. Van Dijk, who is right-footed but also plays on the left side of central defence, would leave a gap for Liverpool to fill should he depart.

The Brazilian centre-back has a contract until December 2028 and has already seen a Tottenham Hotspur offer of £18m (€21m) rejected by Athletico Paranaense. The club’s board believes Arthur Dias should only be released for an offer of at least £25.5m (€30m) because of his high potential.

So far, Liverpool have made no formal approach to Athletico Paranaense for the young defender, but the competition is not limited to Barcelona.

Clubs such as Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are also monitoring Arthur Dias, who gained international visibility with his first two call-ups to the Brazil national team in the post-World Cup international breaks.

Brazilian aside, Liverpool’s number four has no guaranteed future at Anfield. Despite his idol status and undisputed place in the starting line-up under manager Andoni Iraola, Van Dijk has no advanced talks with the club’s directors over his stay, with moves towards an extension expected to gather pace at the turn of the year.

The captain himself admitted in a recent interview that he plans to stay at Liverpool, but has no news on his situation.

The Spanish manager is in favour of Van Dijk staying, as the Dutchman is not only a leadership figure in the dressing room but also a pillar of the defensive system, having won 75% of his duels in this season’s Premier League.

In that context, AC Milan have emerged as one of the clubs interested in the 35-year-old defender. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is an admirer of the Dutchman and believes he can make a difference to Ruben Amorim’s project through his experience and technical quality.

#1927. Lewes down Town to reach Sussex Senior Cup last eight

On a damp evening on the Sussex coast, Lewes defeated Step 4 Town 2-1 to make the last eight.

Two goals of varying difficulty from Bassett laid the foundations for the win, with the Rooks then withstanding Town’s pressure after a Sonny Walsh strike to make progress.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

While it was not the most fluent outing for Lewes, several performances on an evening of experimentation will give reason for optimism.

The Rooks arrived at The Saffrons with six changes to their starting XI, including Josh Spinks’ return as captain and a debut for new attacking signing Kwesi Ntim.

Ntim, who has scored 20 goals in 33 games for Lingfield in 2026, was a bright spark early on, cutting in from the left flank and posing problems for the home defence.

Genuine chances took a while to arrive on the south coast, with the opening stages dominated by safe possession football.

After 25 minutes, however, Lewes created their first threat as Bassett worked space on the right and forced goalkeeper Chris Winterton to punch a cross into the path of Brian Garzon, whose right-footed effort was cleared off the line.

The Rooks slowly built the pressure from here, with Tyler Christian-Law and Mackenzie Richardson driving at goal before the opener soon arrived.

In the 37th minute, Ntim added a flash of brilliance with a pacey drive in from the left, setting up Richardson for a first-time effort at goal. With ex-Rooks ‘keeper Winterton spilling the ball, Bassett was on hand to tap home.

Richardson had another bite at a goal of his own before the break, but Winterton stood up well to a rising effort from the left of the box to keep the score at 0-1.

Lewes did not hesitate in doubling down on their advantage at the start of the second half, and Bassett was the man to deliver again.

Barely 30 seconds into the half, the forward stormed down the right and cut into the box before producing an audacious chip on Winterton that dropped into the top left corner.

It was a moment of magic, and whether Bassett had meant it or not, nobody could begrudge the striker his fourth goal of the season thus far.

The Rooks got into a rhythm after this, regularly wriggling free of Town's attentions and finding space on the counter without truly putting the game to bed.

Bassett and Ntim were similarly denied in the area, while Garzon had at least two notable chances while cutting inside that flew inches wide of the post.

All the while, Town were never out of the tie, and they got their spark in the 61st minute.

Sonny Walsh was set free on the right of the box and blasted an effort past Louis Rogers to halve the deficit.

Town had two brilliant chances to level the scores in the final 30 minutes, but as has been their story in the last few weeks, luck was against them.

A ball in from the right was stabbed over the crossbar from close range, and in the dying stages, Walsh was again set free on the right but blasted over the target.

Equally, Lewes could have added to their advantage as substitute Omar Al-Seadi prodded wide of the left post when excellently teed up by a combination of Bassett and Kurtis Cumberbatch.

Altogether, Lewes were relieved to hear the final whistle as they made it to the final eight, but were good value for the result across the 90 minutes.

At the time of writing, the timing of the draw for the Quarter-Finals, and the dates of this round, are yet to be announced.

We anticipate news of both in due course, and urge supporters to keep tabs on our social media pages for the latest updates.

This Saturday, the Rooks are back in Isthmian Premier Division action away at Ramsgate FC.

With Lewes in 5th and Ramsgate - with a game in hand - just three points behind in 6th, it has all the makings of an excellent game at Southwood Stadium. Kick-off is at 3pm.

#1925. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.
