#1861. Chelsea told to sign £60million Arsenal star instead of Alex Scott

Chelsea should drop their interest in Bournemouth star Alex Scott and turn their attention to a more experienced alternative, according to Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink.

The Blues invested heavily in their squad again during the summer transfer window, but remain light in central midfield where they are heavily reliant on Moises Caicedo following the departures of Enzo Fernandez and Andrey Santos.

Romeo Lavia’s return to form and fitness has represented a welcome boost, but Xabi Alonso is keen to reinforce his engine room further come January.

Scott, who Chelsea attempted to sign in the summer, could well be on the move given his delicate contract situation at Bournemouth.

Arsenal and Liverpool have both been linked with the England international and although Hasselbaink is a keen admirer of the 23-year-old, he feels his old club would be better suited by targeting the Gunners’ out of favour Spain international Martin Zubimendi.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The World Cup winner is yet to start a Premier League game this season amid increased competition as a result of Bruno Guimaraes’ arrival from Newcastle.

Atletico Madrid are understood to have registered their interest in the former Real Sociedad star who is determined to stay and fight for his place at Arsenal, but Hasselbaink believes Chelsea should test the waters.

‘Alex Scott is obviously a top player,’ Hasselbaink told Canada Sports Betting.’He is a player that is getting better with every game that he plays, and he fits with the transfer policy and philosophy of Chelsea because he has serious potential to develop into one of the top midfielders in the world.

‘I would prefer somebody with a little bit more experience because we have so many young players in the squad. I think what Xabi Alonso needs is somebody with more experience who is also a top international.

‘With all due respect to Alex Scott, he is another young player who is good enough but who still has to grow, who’s still learning the game, and he’s in the same bracket as the other players at the club.

‘Chelsea need to go out and sign ready-made winners with proven pedigree because Chelsea need to start winning the big prizes again. The only way to accelerate that is by bringing established players in.

#1860. England's evolution: James Trafford and two other stars chisel their names into the XI, Thomas Tuchel learning from Argentina and Jude Bellingham playing like a captain!

Published: 02:32 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:25 EST, 16 November 2026

England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.

The victory means Thomas Tuchel's side top their Nations League group and it provided a strong riposte to criticism of the manager following the World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was at the Metropolitano Stadium, and here are his FIVE big take-aways…

It would not have mattered had England conceded a late equaliser. To draw comparison with Argentina in the final half hour is unfair and inaccurate. The World Cup semi-final was 11v11 and so, when we draw conclusions from this game, let us do so on the same terms.

Thomas Tuchel was delighted with his England players as they won 3-2 away in Spain

And what did England do at 11v11 with a 1-0 lead? They attacked. And attacked again. This was a major change (and improvement) and is the reason for such encouragement. They have learnt from a mistake, as much as Tuchel will be loathe to admit.

Mexico would be a fairer parallel, but that was against opposition far inferior to Spain. At 11v10, we could not expect England to stay on the front foot here, as they were until the point of Jarell Quansah's needless mistake and Elliot Anderson's subsequent red card.

And that is cause for great optimism - because this game was not in the balance in any way when the teams were at equal number.

For me, and I don't think this is even close, this was the best performance of Tuchel's reign.

Do England suddenly have a pair of full backs?! After years of trawling and trialling, here in the most testing of surrounds, Ben White and Lewis Hall inked their names into Tuchel's XI.

We can forgive the concession of two goals when down to 10 men - because with 11, Spain barely looked like getting a shot on target. In fact, they didn't.

Much of that was down to the solidity of the full backs. Then, with backs to the wall, the pair became bricks in the resistance. One White block late on was heroic.

Before that, Hall's best work was not in containing Lamine Yamal, but in emulating him. His dribbles were daring and unnerved Spain, who thought they would spend the game in England's half and with the ball. They did neither early on and Hall was central to that.

White's goal had shades of Carlos Alberto on the overlap, and his England redemption arc felt like it reached completion here. Let him now move on now, for England need him.

No more boos, please, only cheers for White (and Hall).

It's time to stop the boos for Ben White after he starred with Lewis Hall at full back

Ezri Konsa is England's best defender. Build the backline around him.

Tuchel said on the eve of the game that he thought Konsa had grown for the move to Arsenal, and this was proof.

Boy do England need a mature, reliable presence at the heart of their defence. Konsa showed here why he can be that man. He scored a fine goal, which is always a sign of a defender ready to take wider responsibility, but it was his cool interceptions and desperate blocks at the other end that were most reassuring.

What Konsa has to do now is build on this - and a man-of-the-match performance at the home of the world champions is a pretty lofty and solid foundation from which to do so.

Tuchel will, and should, be giving serious thought to keeping James Trafford in England's goal for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Jordan Pickford has done nothing wrong. And yet, it feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and here was his justification.

Trafford can be a little erratic and immature. What better way to grow, emotionally, than with a series of saves to preserve an historic win. He will feel like a different player, and person, to the one who started this game. Like White and Hall, this felt like a coming-of-age night in an England jersey.

Trafford has all the tools. He might just have used them to chisel his name into that team-sheet.

Goalkeeper feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and James Trafford starred

Spain's fans are left shocked as Ezri Konsa hails the brilliant Trafford in emphatic fashion

No goals, but England would not have won this game without Bellingham. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his brilliance.

Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too.

His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. Of all the positives from this win, it is hard to look past Bellingham as the biggest reason for England being able to challenge Spain at the top of the world rankings.

Jude Bellingham played like a captain, dropping into midfield when down to 10 men

He won the corner for the second goal and created the third. He then dropped into midfield when down to 10 and played like a captain.

That is what England need - Bellingham the leader, not Bellingham the individual. He has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. They don't come much bigger than what England achieved here.

#1859. Barcelona respond as Alejandro Balde pushes for Man Utd transfer

Barcelona have confirmed they have no plans to sell Alejandro Balde and insist the Manchester United-linked left-back remains an ‘important player’ for the club going forward.

Balde has been with Barca since the age of just eight, making a total of 173 appearances in all competitions since breaking into the first-team squad back in 2021.

In that time, the 23-year-old has helped the Catalan giants win seven pieces of silverware, including three La Liga titles – the most recent coming under Hansi Flick last season.

However, Balde has become an increasingly peripheral figure at the Camp Nou in recent months, with all five of his appearances this term coming from the substitutes bench.

Balde currently finds himself behind both Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart in the pecking order at Barca and the Spain international’s career appears to be at a crossroads.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, this has forced Balde to consider his options and the full-back is understood to be keen on joining Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United in January.

Other reports suggest that ‘everything Balde has heard about his situation has come through press conferences’ and the defender views the Premier League as a possible escape route.

The subject of Balde’s future has proven a major talking point both in the media and amongst Barcelona’s fanbase – and the topic was raised during Catalunya Radio’s joint interview with club chiefs Bojan and Deco on Wednesday.

Asked about the possible sale of Balde this winter, football coordinator Bojan replied: ‘Balde is a fantastic lad.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Obviously, he’s in an uncomfortable situation. The player wants to play.

‘He’s one of our own and he’s still an important player. It’s true that he’s not playing right now, although he’s ready if the manager needs him.’

Deco, Barca’s sporting director, was similarly unequivocal when asked if a transfer deal could be on the cards for Balde.

‘No,’ the ex-Barca, Chelsea and Portugal responded.

‘There is also the player’s side, but he hasn’t told us anything about being unhappy, that’s not the case.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United had been actively looking to strengthen at left-back in the summer in order to provide support and competition for Luke Shaw, the club’s only specialist in the position other than academy product Harry Amass.

The Red Devils ultimately failed to bolster their full-back options, though, which has come back to bite them already this season, with Shaw sidelined for the last month through injury.

Diogo Dalot was therefore forced to fill in as a makeshift left-back in the bleak final weeks of Michael Carrick’s tenure at the Theatre of Dreams.

It’s understood Lewis Hall had been identified as United’s number one left-back target ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, but Newcastle made it clear the England international would not be sold for anything other than an astronomical price.

Hall would go on to put pen to paper on a new long-term deal at St James’ Park, tying him to the Magpies until 2031.

Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert, Fulham’s Antonee Robinson, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Crystal Palace’s Tyrick Mitchell have also been linked in recent months.

#1858. Barcelona add £57m Man Utd star to transfer shortlist ahead of January window

Barcelona have Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez on their transfer shortlist ahead of the January window, according to reports.

Martinez is into his fifth season at United after signing from Ajax for £57million in 2022.

The Argentine has made 121 appearances in all competitions for the Red Devils, but is out of contract at the end of the season.

United do have the option to trigger a 12-month extension to Martinez’s contract, but they may have reservations after he launched a scathing public critique of the club’s transfer strategy last month.

And now, Mundo Deportivo reports that Barcelona could be waiting in the wings to pounce as they seek to add a centre-back in the January window.

The report adds that Martinez would be willing to listen to an offer, although the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino as United’s new manager could complicate Barcelona’s pursuit.

#1857. Watch: Pulisic shines as Pochettino news dominates headlines – Captain America bags a brace vs. Haiti

Last night, AC Milan will have been very happy to see Christian Pulisic extending his fine goalscoring form with a brace for America.

The United States national team have certainly faced a rocky few days. Thanks to Manchester United parting ways with Michael Carrick, Mauricio Pochettino will leave his role as the head coach of the project after the international break, leaving them in a strange position currently.

However, that was not a problem for The Stars and The Stripes, who put six past Haiti in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League. Of course, who else would be key but Pulisic himself?

Playing as a number 10 in a 4-2-3-1 system – which will have pleased Milan’s coach, Ruben Amorim – Pulisic was instrumental, scoring a brace in just two minutes. After 62 minutes, he stepped up from the spot after drawing the penalty himself.

Then, just a minute later, he added a second and recorded his 35th goal for the USMNT in 91 appearances.

For the attacker, it extends his fine run of form and the second half of 2026 is proving to be much more fruitful than the first. In Serie A, he’s scored four goals and provided an assist in eight games, and he’s now grabbed two more for the national team. After missing the last camp, it’s another reminder of his importance.

With Pochettino departing, it’s clear that they’ll still be in fine hands, with Pulisic remaining key!

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

A few notes: 1. This first match (of two for the Nations League) was played in Miami, Florida, and counted as a home match for Haiti, as the ongoing gang violence in Haiti made it too dangerous for an international match to be played there.

2. South Florida has a very large Haitian population, and as a result, the stadium looked like it was 90% filled with Haitians and fans of Haiti. So yeah, it was a home match for Haiti.

3. Haiti can be a very physical and challenging team to play against, but two things helped here – they were missing something like five of their starters from their World Cup team, and the ref was actually somewhat decent in calling fouls properly, instead of the usual CONCACAF ref who lets everything go and turns the match into a mixed martial arts no holds barred cage fight.

4. It was only 1-0 at halftime, Haiti was pressing very hard and were very physical. But then they just collapsed after the foul on Pulisic and the PK.

5. The USMNT has never looked this good – as a longtime follower of the USMNT, I can clearly see Pochettino’s influence and his selection of players and his tactics finally coming into fruition. Too bad he is leaving.

6. Poch’s coaching, tactics, and selection of younger players actually look a lot like what Amorim is doing at Milan. And yes, in his first year with the USMNT, Poch took some losses to teams that the USMNT had been able to beat previously. Which should mean that Amorim’s system should start looking great next year.

7. Unfortunately for Pochettino, ManUre are completely packed with players on high wages that are poorly suited for his tactics. As ManUre are in a relegation fight and Poch generally takes at least a year to rebuild a team and fully implement his ideas, I would not be at all be surprised to see ManUre get relegated. Poch is not a specialist in fighting relegation.

Yes, finally a decent ref and a decent field for a Hati home game.
